You must make your appeal request within 65 calendar days from the date on the written notice. [1][2]
For a standard appeal, you can submit your request in writing or by calling the plan. [1]
For a fast appeal, you can submit your request in writing or by calling the plan. [1]
If you miss the appeal deadline, you can explain the reason for the delay, and the plan may grant more time. [1]
You can ask for a copy of the information regarding your medical decision and add more information to support your appeal. [1]

A grievance is also called a complaint. [1]
Filing a grievance is the process of making a complaint. [1]
An expedited grievance is called a fast complaint. [1]
To file a grievance, you can contact Member Services by phone at 1-888-778-1478 (TTY users call 711). [1]
You can also file a grievance in writing if you prefer not to call or are unsatisfied after calling. [1]
If you file a grievance in writing, Clover Health will respond to your complaint in writing. [1]
A representative can file a grievance on your behalf if they have legal authorization or an Appointment of Representative form. [1]
The grievance process is used for problems related to quality of care, waiting times, customer service, and other issues not involving coverage decisions or appeals. [2]

You can get care from out-of-network providers, but your share of the costs may be higher. [1]
Out-of-network providers are not obligated to treat you unless it is an emergency. [1]
If you use an out-of-network provider who is not eligible to participate in Medicare, you will be responsible for the full cost of services. [1]
You do not need a referral or prior authorization to see out-of-network providers. [1]
It is recommended to ask for a pre-visit coverage decision to confirm that services from out-of-network providers are covered and medically necessary. [1]
If you pay for covered services from an out-of-network provider, you can request reimbursement for our share of the cost. [1]
If you use an out-of-network provider for emergency care, urgently needed services, or out-of-area dialysis, you may not have to pay a higher cost-sharing amount. [1]
